gbm_population_evidence.quote: Grade III Astrocytoma; Grade IV Astrocytoma; Astrocytoma, Grade IV; Astrocytoma, Grade III
Histologically proven diagnosis of newly diagnosed supratentorial high-grade astrocytoma (WHO grade III-IV), excluding astrocytoma of brainstem and cerebellum.
Gliosarcoma or other subvariants are allowed, including the newly defined "diffuse astrocytoma, IDH-wildtype, with molecular features of glioblastoma, WHO grade IV" (Brat et al., 2018).

candidate_evidence.quote: The purpose of this study is to investigate the impact of targeting MDSCs in newly diagnosed IDH-wildtype grade III-IV astrocytoma by combining tadalafil with standard of care radiation therapy (RT) and temozolomide (TMZ).

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Histologically proven diagnosis of newly diagnosed supratentorial high-grade astrocytoma (WHO grade III-IV), excluding astrocytoma of brainstem and cerebellum.

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: Relative change of MDSCs in peripheral blood

Tadalafil, an FDA-approved drug with inexpensive cost and excellent safety profile, has been shown to effectively reduce MDSCs and restore T-cell activation in the peripheral blood and in the tumor microenvironment.

coder_notes: Population: newly diagnosed IDH-wildtype WHO grade III-IV astrocytoma; grade IV astrocytoma (conditions) and 'molecular features of glioblastoma' (inclusion) name glioblastoma, while grade III is also eligible, so mixed_glioma_gbm_named. IDH-wildtype required (IDH-mutant excluded) so cns5 terminology, though WHO 2016-era wording (Brat 2018, grade III/IV) is also used. Temozolomide not a registered intervention but given to all per standard of care. Target engagement: primary outcome is change in peripheral-blood MDSCs, the stated tadalafil mechanism. Tumour-treating fields permitted per routine care (device, not listed). Heterogeneity diffusion imaging outcome is imaging only.
